newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt surplus NZ$743 mln in 3 months to Sept.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt surplus NZ$743 mln in 3 months to Sept.

text.p: The New Zealand government said on Friday it posted a NZ$743 million operating budget surplus for the three months to September 30, 1996, against a forecast surplus of $682 million.
Net public debt as a percentage of GDP was 30.9 percent at September 30 against 32.4 percent at June 30.
Total revenue was $9 million, 0.1 percent, lower than forecast while expenses were $6 million, 0.1 percent, lower than forecast.
The government's net worth at September 30 was $4.29 billion, $267 million better than forecast and $949 million better than at June 30.
Treasury said the reasons for the $61 million budget improvement on forecast were:
* The net surplus, less distributions attributable to State-owned Enterprises was $64 million, 48 percent above forecast.

* Non-taxation revenue was $31 million, 4.7 percent, higher than forecast, largely due to higher-than-forecast sales of goods and services and other operational revenue. Partly offsetting those was lower-than-forecast taxation revenue, $40 million or 0.5 percent, largely due to lower-than-forecast source deductions revenue, and petroleum fuels excise duty.
Net public debt was $27.26 billion, $84 million lower than forecast and $1.37 billion lower than at June 30.

The lower debt was principally due to the proceeds from the sale of Forestry Corp of New Zealand. It was lower than forecast due to lower-than-forecast cash outflows from operations ($45 million) and lower than forecast net purchases of physical assets ($36 million).

Net cash flows from operating and investing activities were an outflow of $373 million, compared with a forecast inflow of $137 million mainly due to the $527 million higher-than-forecast net purchases of marketable securities and deposits.
